description_ru: Вымышленный выпуск новостей о сильной жаре в северной стране и советах метеорологов.
text:
Northern Valdia has recorded its hottest day in history, as temperatures reached thirty-nine degrees in the capital, Lorenburg. Weather experts say the heatwave will continue for at least another four days.

Meteorologist Dr Karen Osei explained that a mass of warm air from the south has been sitting over the region since last Monday. "We have never seen such high temperatures so early in the summer," she told reporters. "Unless a cold front arrives, the heat will become even more dangerous."

Hospitals have reported a rise in the number of patients with heat exhaustion, especially among elderly people. The health ministry has advised everyone to drink plenty of water, stay in the shade during the afternoon, and avoid exercise outdoors. Parents have been told never to leave children or pets in a parked car.

Meanwhile, life in the capital has slowed down. Many shops now open at dawn and close at noon, and the city has set up fifty cooling centres in libraries and schools. At the central swimming pool, queues stretched around the block, and ice cream sellers say they have never been so busy.

Farmers are worried too. If the rain does not return soon, they warn, the wheat harvest could be much smaller than expected, and food prices may rise.

Forecasters say that relief may come on Friday, when thunderstorms are expected to move in from the west. Until then, residents are asked to look after their neighbours.
